Company in accordance with local custom) and shall be re-prorated following receipt of the actual bill
with respect to the applicable period. Allocation of real estate taxes billed with respect to the Assets to
yearly periods shall be determined in accordance with local custom, as determined by the Title Company.

                          (b)      All charges and payments for utility services; provided that if there is no
meter or if the current bill for any of such utilities has not been issued prior to the Closing Date, then such
charges shall be adjusted at the Closing on the basis of the charges for the prior period for which bills
were issued and shall be further adjusted when the bills for the current period are issued; provided further,
to the extent possible, Sellers shall terminate their accounts with the utility service providers and
Purchaser shall establish its accounts with such utility service providers effective on the Closing Date, in
which event, there shall be no proration for such utility services.

                         (c)      The obligations of the parties hereto under this Section 8.5 shall survive
the Closing.

         9.       RISK OF LOSS; CONDEMNATION. In the event there is any material damage,
destruction or loss with respect to any of the Assets, whether by fire, theft, vandalism, condemnation or
other cause or casualty, between the date hereof and the Closing Date, (i) Purchaser shall have the right to
terminate this Agreement by giving Property Seller written notice of its intention to do so, such notice by
Purchaser to Property Seller to be given not later than ten (10) Business Days after Purchaser shall have
received the notice from Sellers of such aforesaid occurrence (whereupon the Deposit, plus accrued
interest thereon, shall be returned to Purchaser and this Agreement shall terminate and be of no further
force or effect whatsoever except with respect to those rights and obligations, if any, which specifically
survive termination of this Agreement) or (ii) if Purchaser elects not to terminate this Agreement, then
Sellers shall assign the insurance proceeds or condemnation award, as applicable, on account of such
damage or loss to Purchaser, to the extent necessary to complete the repairs, and this transaction shall be
closed without a reduction in the Purchase Price. For the purposes of this Section 9, “material damage,
destruction or loss,” shall mean damage to, or condemnation of, the Facility, the costs of repair for which
exceeds Four Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars ($420,000), or which, in Purchaser’s reasonable
judgment, renders the Facility less than a functional structure to continue to operate the business at the
Facility at at least 90% its licensed capacity.

        10.      INDEMNIFICATION; REMEDIES.

                 10.1    Survival; Right to Indemnification.

                         (a)       All representations, warranties and covenants in this Agreement and the
OTA and a party’s right to recover Damages resulting from a breach of such representation, warranty or
covenant shall survive Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of eighteen (18) months
following the Closing; provided that the representations and warranties set forth in Sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.8,
3.10, 3.15, 3.16, 3.19, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4 of this Agreement and Sections 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2 of the
OTA, and Section 2.17 of the OTA regarding Excluded Liabilities (collectively, the “Fundamental
Provisions”) shall survive until thirty (30) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations
with respect to the matters covered thereunder. All of the other covenants and obligations of the parties
contained in this Agreement or the OTA to be performed after Closing shall survive the Closing for
eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date, except for any provisions in this Agreement, including, but
not limited to, the indemnity covenants set forth in this Section 10, and provisions in the OTA that
expressly contain a longer survival period. For the avoidance of doubt, any survival periods set forth in
this Section 10.1(a) shall be subject to and interpreted in accordance with Section 6.10 of the OTA. The
provisions of this Section 10 shall survive the Closing.

                 10.2    Indemnification by Sellers.

                          (a)     Subject to the consummation of a Closing hereunder, Sellers shall
indemnify and defend Purchaser, Purchaser’s Operator, their Affiliates, and their respective
representatives (collectively, the “Purchaser Indemnified Parties”) against, and hold all of them harmless
from, all Damages (the “Purchaser Indemnified Losses”) arising, directly or indirectly, from or in
connection with (i) any breach of any representation or warranty made by Sellers in this Agreement or by
Existing Operator in the OTA; (ii) any breach by Sellers or Existing Operator, as applicable, of any
covenant, agreement or obligation of Sellers or Existing Operator, as applicable, in this Agreement or the
OTA; (iii) any claims, demands, investigations, actions, suits, judicial or administrative Proceedings, or
arbitrations by any third party arising out of allegations that, if true, would constitute a breach of, or
material inaccuracy in, any representation or warranty referenced in clause (i) or a failure to perform any
covenant, agreement or obligation referenced in clause (ii) of this Section 10.2; (iv) any Liability of
Sellers not expressly assumed hereunder or under the OTA; (v) any and all claims brought by a third party
against any Purchaser Indemnified Party in connection with the ownership of the Facility by Property
Seller prior to the Closing Date; (vi) any and all claims brought by a third party against any Purchaser
Indemnified Party in connection with the use or the operation of the Facility by Existing Operator prior to
the Closing Date; and (vii) any determination by Medicare or Medicaid, any fiscal intermediary, or any
federal or state Governmental Body or any private third party payors that any amounts paid to Existing
Operator by Medicare or Medicaid, any fiscal intermediary, or any federal or state Governmental Body
for any services provided by Existing Operator at the Facility prior to the Closing Date resulted in an
overpayment or other determination by Medicare or Medicaid, any fiscal intermediary, or any federal or
state Governmental Body that funds previously paid by Medicare or Medicaid, any fiscal intermediary, or
any federal or state Governmental Body to Existing Operator must be repaid, which determination results
in (x) an offset against amounts owed to Purchaser or Purchaser’s Operator, or (y) any penalty, sanction
or repayment obligations being assessed against Purchaser or Purchaser’s Operator.

                         (b)    Except as otherwise set forth in this Agreement, in no event shall the
aggregate Liability for indemnification claims paid by Sellers pursuant to this Section 10.2 exceed Two
Hundred Fifty Thousand and no/100 Dollars ($250,000.00) (the “Cap”), nor shall Sellers be liable for any
indemnification obligation under this Section 10.2 unless the aggregate amount of Purchaser Indemnified
                                                      27

Losses hereunder and under the OTA exceeds Fifty Thousand and no/100 Dollars ($50,000.00) (the
“Basket”), at which time Sellers shall be liable for the amount of any Purchaser Indemnified Losses from

Purchaser Indemnified Loss arising under Section 10.2(a)(iv), Section 10.2(a)(v), Section 10.2(a)(vi),

                10.4 Duty to Mitigate. Each Person entitled to indemnification pursuant to Section

indemnification may be sought pursuant to this Section 10.

                10.5    Indemnity Claims.

                          (a)      If any claim (“Claim”) is asserted by a party as to which such party may
be entitled to indemnification hereunder, such party (an “Indemnified Party”) shall notify (“Claims
Notice”) the other party required by the terms of this Agreement to indemnify the Indemnified Party (an
“Indemnifying Party”) within ten (10) Business Days; provided, however, the failure or delay by an
Indemnified Party to give a prompt Claims Notice (if given prior to the expiration of any applicable
survival periods) shall not release, waive or otherwise affect an Indemnifying Party’s obligations with
respect to the Claim, except to the extent that the Indemnifying Party can demonstrate actual material loss
or prejudice as a result of such failure or delay.

                       (b)      The Claims Notice shall describe the Claim and the specific facts and
circumstances in reasonable detail and shall indicate the amount, if known, or an estimate, if possible, of
Damages that have been or may be incurred or suffered (the “Claim Amount”).

                        (c)    The Indemnifying Party shall defend or compromise any claim by a third
party (“Third Party Claim”), at its own expense and by its own counsel, who shall be reasonably
acceptable to the Indemnified Party. The Indemnified Party may participate, at its own expense, in the
defense of any Claim assumed by the Indemnifying Party. Without the approval of the Indemnified Party,
which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, the Indemnifying Party shall not
compromise a Claim defended by the Indemnifying Party which would require the Indemnified Party to
perform or take any action or to refrain from performing or taking any action or to pay any additional
Persons in the future.

                           (d)    Notwithstanding anything in this Section 10.5 to the contrary, if an
Indemnified Party determines in good faith that there is a reasonable probability that a Proceeding will
affect it or its Affiliates adversely other than as a result of monetary Damages for which it would be
entitled to indemnification under this Agreement, the Indemnified Party may, by notice to the
Indemnifying Party, assume the exclusive right to defend, compromise, or settle such Proceeding at the
cost of the Indemnifying Party, but the Indemnifying Party will not be bound by any determination of a
Proceeding so defended or any compromise or settlement effected without its consent (which may not be
unreasonably withheld or delayed).

                        (e)     If, within ten (10) Business Days of the Indemnifying Party’s receipt of a
Claims Notice involving a Third Party Claim, the Indemnifying Party has not notified the Indemnified
Party that the Indemnifying Party will assume the defense, the Indemnified Party may assume control of
the defense or compromise of such Claim, and the costs and expenses of such defense, including costs of
investigation and reasonable attorneys’ fees, shall be added to the Claim. The Indemnified Party shall
have the right to compromise such Claim without the consent of the Indemnifying Party.

                         (f)     The party assuming the defense of any Claim shall keep the other party
reasonably informed at all times of the progress and development of the party’s defense of and
compromise efforts related to such Claim and shall furnish the other party with copies of all relevant
pleadings, correspondence and other papers. In addition, the parties shall reasonably cooperate with each
other, and make available to each other and their representatives all available relevant records or other
materials required by them for their use in defending, compromising or contesting any Claim.

                       (g)     Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, the amount
of any Purchaser Indemnified Losses or Seller Indemnified Losses subject to indemnification under this
Agreement or the OTA shall be calculated net of (i) any insurance proceeds actually received by
Indemnified Party on account of such Purchaser Indemnified Losses or Seller Indemnified Losses and/or
                                                    29

===== PAGE 87 =====
(ii) any indemnification payments actually received from any third party. Anything herein to the contrary
notwithstanding, no Indemnified Party shall have the right to be indemnified for any Purchaser
Indemnified Losses or Seller Indemnified Losses to the extent they are in the nature of consequential,
incidental or indirect damages, diminution in value damages, lost profits or punitive, special or exemplary
damages, and in particular, without limitation, no “multiple of profits” or “multiple of cash flow” or
similar valuation methodology shall be used in calculating the amount of any Purchaser Indemnified
Losses or Seller Indemnified Losses, other than (x) reasonable legal and accounting fees and expenses as
contemplated hereby, to the extent same are deemed to constitute consequential damages, and (y) any
such Purchaser Indemnified Losses or Seller Indemnified Losses that are included in any Third Party
Claim.

                         (h)     If the Seller Indemnified Parties deliver a Claim Notice to Purchaser (a
“Seller Claim Notice”) prior to the expiration of the applicable survival period, Purchaser shall respond to
such Seller Claim Notice (a “Seller Claim Response”) within twenty (20) Business Days (the “Seller
Claim Response Period”) after the date that the Seller Claim Notice is received. Any Seller Claim Notice
or Seller Claim Response shall be given in accordance with the notice requirements hereunder, and any
Seller Claim Response shall specify whether or not the Claim described in the related Seller Claim Notice
is disputed (a “Seller Claim Dispute Notice”). If Purchaser fails to give a Seller Claim Response within
the Seller Claim Response Period or do not dispute the Claim described in a Seller Claim Notice, then the
Claim shall be deemed to be accepted and, if Purchaser does not pay the Claim Amount prior to the end
of the Seller Claim Response Period, the Seller Indemnified Parties may pursue whatever legal remedies
may be available to recover the Claim Amount as to which the Seller Indemnified Parties are seeking
indemnification.

                          (i)     In the event that any Claim asserted by any Seller Indemnified Party is
subject to a Seller Claim Dispute Notice, such Claim shall become an “Unresolved Seller Claim”.
Purchaser and the Seller Indemnified Parties shall attempt in good faith to mutually agree upon the
validity and amount of the Unresolved Seller Claim pursuant to discussions between senior
representatives of the parties who have authority to settle the same. Such discussions shall commence
between the parties not more than ten (10) Business Days following delivery of the Seller Claim Dispute
Notice and shall not last for more than ten (10) Business Days following the date of commencement of
such discussions. In the event that the parties mutually agree upon the amount of the Unresolved Seller
Claim pursuant to such discussions (the “Resolved Seller Claim”), and the Purchaser does not pay the
amount of the Resolved Seller Claim to the Seller Indemnified Parties within five (5) Business Days
thereafter, the Seller Indemnified Parties may pursue whatever legal remedies may be available to recover
the amount of the Resolved Seller Claim. If through negotiation the parties are unable to agree upon the
validity and amount of the Unresolved Seller Claim within thirty (30) calendar days after the
commencement of the negotiations, the dispute shall be referred to litigation in accordance with Section
11.2. In the event that a final and non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction upholds
all or a portion of the amount of an Unresolved Seller Claim (the “Seller Judgment Claim”) and the
Purchaser does not pay the amount of the Seller Judgment Claim to the Seller Indemnified Parties within
five (5) Business Days after the judgment becomes final and non-appealable, the Seller Indemnified
Parties may pursue whatever legal remedies may be available to recover such Seller Judgment Claim
amount.

                       (j)     If the Purchaser Indemnified Parties deliver a Claim Notice to Sellers (a
“Purchaser Claim Notice”) prior to the expiration of the applicable survival period, the Sellers shall
respond to any such Purchaser Claim Notice (a “Purchaser Claim Response”) within twenty (20) Business
Days (the “Purchaser Claim Response Period”) after the date that the Purchaser Claim Notice is received.
Any Purchaser Claim Notice or Purchaser Claim Response shall be given in accordance with the notice
requirements hereunder, and any Purchaser Claim Response shall specify whether or not the Claim
                                                    30

===== PAGE 88 =====
described in the related Purchaser Claim Notice is disputed (a “Purchaser Claim Dispute Notice”). If the
Sellers fail to give a Purchaser Claim Response within the Purchaser Claim Response Period or do not
dispute the Claim described in a Purchaser Claim Notice, then the Purchaser Claim shall be deemed to be
accepted, and, if Seller does not pay the Claim Amount within five (5) days after the expiration of the
Purchaser Claim Response Period, the Purchaser Indemnified Parties may pursue whatever legal remedies
may be available to recover the Claim Amount as to which the Purchaser is seeking indemnification.

                         (k)     In the event that any Claim asserted by any Purchaser Indemnified Party
is subject to a Purchaser Claim Dispute Notice such Claim shall become an “Unresolved Purchaser
Claim”. The Purchaser Indemnified Parties and the Sellers shall attempt in good faith to mutually agree
upon the validity and amount of the Unresolved Purchaser Claim pursuant to discussions between senior
representatives of the parties who have authority to settle the same. Such discussions shall commence
between the parties not more than ten (10) Business Days following delivery of the Purchaser Claim
Dispute Notice and shall not last for more than ten (10) Business Days following the date of
commencement of such discussions. In the event that the parties mutually agree upon the amount of the
Unresolved Purchaser Claim pursuant to such discussions (the “Resolved Purchaser Claim”), the Sellers
shall pay the Purchaser Indemnified Parties the amount of such Resolved Purchaser Claim. If the amount
of such Resolved Purchaser Claim is not paid by or on behalf of Sellers to the Purchaser Indemnified
Parties within five (5) Business Days thereafter, the Purchaser Indemnified Parties may pursue whatever
legal remedies may be available to recover the amount of the Resolved Purchaser Claim. If through
negotiation the parties are unable to agree upon the validity and amount of the Unresolved Purchaser
Claim within thirty (30) calendar days after the commencement of the negotiations, the dispute shall be
referred to litigation in accordance with Section 11.2. In the event that a final and non-appealable
judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction upholds all or a portion of the amount of an Unresolved
Purchaser Claim (the “Purchaser Judgment Claim”) and amount of the Purchaser Judgment Claim is not
paid by or on behalf of the Sellers to the Purchaser Indemnified Parties within five (5) Business Days
after the judgment becomes final and non-appealable, the Purchaser Indemnified Parties may pursue
whatever legal remedies may be available to recover such Purchaser Judgment Claim amount.

the invalidity or unenforceability of any provision shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the
other provisions hereof. If any provision of this Agreement, or the application thereof to any party or any
circumstance, is invalid or unenforceable, (a) a suitable and equitable provision shall be substituted
therefore in order to carry out, so far as may be valid and enforceable, the intent and purpose of such
invalid or unenforceable provision and (b) the remainder of this Agreement and the application of such
provision to the parties or circumstances shall not be affected by such invalidity or unenforceability, nor
shall such invalidity or unenforceability of such provision, or the application thereof, in any other
jurisdiction.

          This BILL OF SALE (this “Instrument”) dated as of August [___], 2019, is made and delivered
pursuant to, and subject to the terms of, that certain Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of August [__],
2019 (as amended and restated from time to time, the “APA”), by and among 740 Oak Hill Road Property
LLC (“Seller”), and certain of its affiliates and Hill Valley Healthcare, LLC (“Purchaser”), and certain
of its affiliates relating to the transfer of certain Assets set forth in the APA in connection with that certain
healthcare facility known as South County Nursing and Rehabilitation Center (the “Facility”).
Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meaning provided in the APA.


                                               WITNESSETH:


        WHEREAS, the Purchaser has the right to acquire the Assets related to the Facility from the
Seller under the APA, excluding therefrom the Excluded Assets, including, without limitation, those
Assets described on Schedule 1 attached hereto (the “Purchased Property”); and


        WHEREAS, Seller and Purchaser desire to evidence and effectuate the transfer and conveyance
of the Purchased Property to Purchaser.


        NOW THEREFORE, subject to the terms and conditions of the APA and for good and valuable
consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, Seller and Purchaser hereby
agree as follows:


        1.      Subject to the terms of the APA, Seller does hereby convey, transfer, assign and deliver
to Purchaser all of Seller’s right, title and interest in and the Purchased Property, free of all liens,
encumbrances and security interests, and the Purchaser hereby accepts from Seller all of the Purchased
Property. Specifically excluded from this Bill of Sale shall be those items described and defined as
Excluded Assets under the APA.


         2.      Subject to the terms of the APA, Purchaser hereby assumes all liabilities and obligations
related to the Purchased Property with respect to periods from and after the date hereof.


        3.      This Instrument shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and its
respective successors and assigns.

                                                                 EXECUTION VERSION


                         OPERATIONS TRANSFER AGREEMENT

  This OPERATIONS TRANSFER AGREEMENT (“Agreement”) is entered into as February
28, 2020 (“Effective Date”), by and between 740 Oak Hill Road Operations LLC, a Rhode Island
limited liability company (“Existing Operator”), and South County SNF Operations LLC, a
Rhode Island limited liability company (“New Operator”), and solely for purposes of Section 5,
Genesis Healthcare, Inc., a Delaware Corporation (“Guarantor”).
                                           RECITALS

        A.      740 Oak Hill Road Property LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company and
an affiliate of Existing Operator (“Seller”) owns that certain nursing facility located at 740 Oak
Hill Road, North Kingstown, Rhode Island and commonly known as “South County Nursing and
Rehabilitation Center” (the “Facility”). The Facility is licensed for 120 skilled nursing facility
beds.

       B.      Seller leases the Facility to an affiliate of Seller and Existing Operator, who then
subleases the Facility to Existing Operator pursuant to that certain Lease Agreement December
1, 2015.

        C.      Seller is a party to that certain Asset Purchase Agreement, dated as of even date
herewith (the “APA”), by and between Seller and New Operator (in the context of the APA, the
“Purchaser”), pursuant to which Purchaser shall purchase from Seller substantially all of Seller’s
assets related to the Facility.

        D.      Guarantor has agreed to guarantee certain obligations of Existing Operator and
Seller, as further described in the APA.

        E.    Simultaneously with the consummation of the transfer of operations contemplated
by this Agreement, New Operator will lease the Facility from Purchaser. The Facility is to be
used by New Operator for the operation of a skilled nursing facility, with licenses issued to New
Operator pursuant to applicable law.

       F.      In conjunction with the execution of the APA, Existing Operator and New
Operator desire to enter into this Agreement to facilitate an orderly transition of the Facility’s
operations from Existing Operator to New Operator.

       G.     Certain capitalized terms used herein have the meanings given to them on Exhibit
A attached hereto. Any capitalized terms used herein and not otherwise defined shall have the
meanings given to them in the APA.

                                         AGREEMENT

  NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises contained herein, and for other
good and valuable consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which are hereby acknowledged,
the parties hereto agree that:

                            SECTION 1
PRE-CLOSING; CONDITIONS TO CLOSING; DELIVERIES UPON CLOSING DATE

1.1    Pre-Closing.

       (a)     Between the Effective Date and the earlier to occur of the Closing Date
(notwithstanding any consummation of the transactions contemplated under the APA prior to the
Closing hereunder) or the termination of the APA and this Agreement, New Operator is and shall
be an intended third party beneficiary of each and every affirmative and negative covenant of
Existing Operator set forth in the APA including, but not limited to, those set forth in Sections
5.4 and 5.5 thereof.

        (b)    New Operator will use its good faith efforts to promptly obtain all Government
Authorizations necessary to operate the Facility, including, without limitation, by complying
with its covenants set forth in Section 2.2 hereof.

1.2     Conditions to Closing. The consummation of the transactions contemplated hereunder
(the “Closing”) and the obligations of Existing Operator and New Operator under this
Agreement that are to be performed on the day on which the Closing occurs (the “Closing Date”)
shall be subject to the following conditions precedent on, and as of, the Closing Date, to the
reasonable satisfaction of or the waiver thereof by the party benefitting from such condition, in
the absence of which the benefitting party may terminate this Agreement (following written
notice to the other party and ten (10) business days to cure such failure):

        (a)    the transactions contemplated by the APA shall have closed prior to or be closing
simultaneously with the Closing hereunder, it being understood and agreed that, other than those
rights granted to and obligations imposed on Existing Operator and/or New Operator which are
specifically required to be performed prior to the Closing, neither Existing Operator nor New
Operator shall have any rights or obligations hereunder if the closing of the transactions set forth
in the APA fail to occur;

         (b)    New Operator shall have received from the appropriate governmental authorities
all licenses, certificates, permits and approvals required for the operation of the Facility by New
Operator, including, without limitation, a Consent Order (the “Consent Order”) from the Rhode
Island Department of Health (collectively, the “Licenses”), or otherwise shall have confirmed the
approval from the appropriate governmental authorities for the issuance of such Licenses to New
Operator effective as of the Closing Date upon receipt of evidence of the transfer of the Facility
to New Operator;

       (c)     No Facility shall have had any operating license revoked, suspended, placed on
probation, or otherwise disciplined or limited, or have been decertified, suspended, or limited
from, or otherwise deemed ineligible for (whether permanently or temporarily), participation in
the Medicare and/or Medicaid reimbursement program;

        (d)    Since the date of this Agreement, there shall have occurred, no event,
circumstance or other change in Existing Operator, its assets, or the Facility that, alone or in the
aggregate, constitutes a Material Adverse Effect that has not been corrected or resolved on or
prior to Closing to New Operator’s satisfaction as determined in its reasonable discretion;

                                      SECTION 2
                                TRANSFER OF OPERATIONS

2.1     Cooperation. The parties hereto agree to cooperate with each other to effect an orderly
transfer of the operation of the Facility on the Closing Date. In furtherance and not in limitation
of the foregoing, New Operator shall have the same rights of access and inspection prior to the
Closing Date as are granted to Purchaser under the APA. Further, following the Effective Date,
Existing Operator shall cooperate with New Operator, and use commercially reasonable efforts
to furnish all requested documentation in Existing Operator’s possession or control, and execute
all documents and consents reasonably necessary, for New Operator to obtain the Health Care
Licenses, other than Existing Operator’s Medicaid provider agreements, all at no cost or expense
to Existing Operator other than as provided in Section 2.13 hereof.

2.2     Licensure. New Operator shall use commercially reasonable efforts to transfer or obtain
new Licenses. New Operator shall file such applications and provide any required Medicaid
notices within all legally required timeframes prior to the Closing Date. Existing Operator shall
cooperate with New Operator to take all actions necessary for New Operator to transfer or obtain
the new Licenses as required for the operation of the Facility by New Operator as of the Closing
Date, and, in that regard, Existing Operator agrees, promptly upon request by New Operator, to
execute any reasonably necessary documents or notifications required in connection with such
efforts. Existing Operator agrees to promptly provide or make available to New Operator for
photocopying, upon request, to the extent such documentation is within Existing Operator’s
possession or control, any and all existing documentation requested by New Operator necessary
for the issuance of the new Licenses. Existing Operator agrees to use commercially reasonable
efforts to cooperate with New Operator in obtaining any other approval from a Governmental
Entity that is required as a result of the transactions contemplated hereby.

2.3    Patient Funds; Advance Payments.

       (a)    Prior to the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall prepare a Resident Census
Report. Within thirty (30) days following the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall update the
Resident Census Report to reflect the residents at the Facility as of the Closing Date.

        (b)    Prior to the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall prepare a true, correct and
complete accounting, properly reconciled, of any Resident Trust Funds then held by Existing
Operator for residents at the Facility. On the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall transfer the
Resident Trust Funds to bank accounts designated by New Operator, and New Operator shall, in
writing, acknowledge receipt of and expressly assume all of Existing Operator’s financial and
custodial obligations with respect to such Resident Trust Funds actually delivered by Existing
Operator, it being the intent and purpose of this provision that, at the Closing, Existing Operator
will be relieved of all fiduciary and custodial obligation with respect to such Resident Trust
Funds actually delivered to New Operator, and that New Operator will assume all such
obligations and be directly accountable to the residents with respect thereto. Within thirty (30)
days following the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall update such accounting, properly

                                                5

===== PAGE 135 =====
reconciled, as of the Closing Date. The provisions of this Section 2.3(b) shall survive the
Closing as provided in Section 5.

         (c)     Existing Operator will indemnify, defend and hold New Operator harmless for,
from and against all liabilities, claims, demands and settlements, including, without limitation,
reasonable attorneys’ fees, (i) in the event the amount of the Resident Trust Funds, if any,
transferred to New Operator does not constitute the full amount of the Resident Trust Funds that
were to be delivered to New Operator, (ii) as a result of inaccuracies in the accounting of
Resident Trust Funds provided by Existing Operator, or (iii) for claims which arise from actions
or omissions of Existing Operator with respect to the Resident Trust Funds prior to or after the
Closing Date. New Operator agrees to indemnify and hold Existing Operator harmless from all
liabilities, claims, demands and settlements, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys’
fees that may be asserted against Existing Operator in connection with New Operator’s custody
and treatment from and after the Closing Date of the Resident Trust Funds delivered by Existing
Operator to New Operator. This Section 2.3(c) shall survive the Closing as provided in Section
5.

2.4    Employees.

         (a)     At a time mutually agreed to by Existing Operator and New Operator prior to the
Closing Date, New Operator shall notify the Employees of the transactions contemplated in this
Agreement (the “Employee Notification”). Prior to the Employee Notification, New Operator
shall not meet or talk to any Employees except as specifically agreed to by Existing Operator in
its sole discretion. Following the Employee Notification, New Operator shall be entitled to meet
and talk to the Employees at times reasonably agreed upon by the parties.

         (b)    Concurrently with the delivery of the Employee Notification, Existing Operator
shall notify the Employees employed by it or its affiliates that they will terminate their
employment as of 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the day prior to the Closing Date. In New
Operator’s sole discretion, New Operator may offer full-time and part-time Employees at the
Facility employment with New Operator with benefits similar to what New Operators provide to
their current employees in similar capacities; provided, however, that New Operator shall not be
entitled to offer employment to those certain Employees listed on Schedule 2.4(b) hereto, whom
New Operator acknowledges have been offered employment with Existing Operator or its
affiliates following the Closing Date and have accepted such offer of employment. Those
persons who receive and accept an offer of employment are referred to herein as the
“Transitioned Employees”. Notwithstanding the foregoing, New Operator shall not be obligated
to hire any employee not approved by New Operator, including, without limitation, any
employee who does not meet New Operator’s current standards for employment. Existing
Operator shall take such action as required by law necessary for Existing Operator to maintain all
liability for non-Transitioned Employees’ health benefits under the Consolidated Omnibus
Budget Reconciliation Act (“COBRA”). Existing Operator acknowledges and agrees that New
Operator is not assuming any of Existing Operator’s obligations to its employees and/or qualified
beneficiaries under COBRA or otherwise, except as specifically provided in this Agreement.

      (c)    Notwithstanding the foregoing, New Operator shall offer employment to such
number of the Employees, and upon such terms and conditions of employment, so as not to

constitute a mass layoff or a plant closing under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining
Notification (“WARN”) Act, 29 U.S.C. § 2101 et seq. The parties do not anticipate that the
transactions contemplated by this Agreement will trigger obligations under the WARN Act, or
under any similar provision of any federal, state, regional, foreign, or local law, rule, or
regulation (referred to collectively as “WARN Obligations”). To the extent that any WARN

        (d)     As soon as practicable following the most recent payroll date prior to the Closing

pay, (3) all benefits that Existing Operator is obligated by all Legal Requirements, its policies, or
both, to provide the Employees as of the Payroll Date, and (4) Existing Operator’s liability for

        (e)    At least ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date, New Operator may elect, in its
sole discretion, to assume the liability for fifty percent (50%) of the ETO of the Transitioned

for the Assumed ETO of Transitioned Employees, (i) New Operator shall be responsible for the
Assumed ETO of all Transitioned Employees on and after the Closing Date; and (ii) Existing
Operator shall pay to New Operator on the Closing Date the amount of such Assumed ETO,
subject to adjustment following the Closing Date in accordance with Section 2.7 hereof. In the
event that New Operator elects not to assume the liability for the Assumed ETO, Existing
Operator shall pay to each Employee of the Facility who is not subject to a Collective Bargaining
Agreement, including the Transitioned Employees, on or prior to the first payroll date following
the Closing Date, an amount equal to such Employee’s Assumed ETO. In addition, on or prior
to the first payroll date following the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall pay out to all
Transitioned Employees who are subject to a Collective Bargaining Agreement all amounts
required to be paid to such Transitioned Employees upon termination of such Transitioned
Employees pursuant to the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreement and in accordance with
all legal requirements. Existing Operator shall be responsible for paying or providing all
applicable Employees with all other benefits to be provided to such Employees for all periods
prior to the Closing Date, including, without limitation, all ETO of Transitioned Employees
which does not constitute Assumed ETO.

        (f)     Upon reasonable advance written notice to New Operator and at reasonable times
that will not unreasonably interfere with the business of New Operator at the Facility, New
Operator agrees to provide Existing Operator with reasonable access to the Facility’s employees
after the Closing Date if necessary for Existing Operator’s defense of any professional liability or
general liability litigation. The provisions of this Section 2.4(f) shall survive the Closing as
provided in Section 5.

         (g)     For a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, neither Existing

         (h)    For a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, neither Purchaser

affiliates, other than the Transitioned Employees, or encourage any such employee(s) to leave

agrees that in the event of a breach or a threatened breach by New Operator or Purchaser of any
such obligations, Existing Operator shall, in addition to any and all other rights and remedies that
may be available to it in respect of such breach, be entitled to equitable relief, including a

New Operator and Purchaser acknowledge that the restrictions contained in this Section 2.4(h)
are reasonable and necessary to protect the legitimate interests of Existing Operator and
constitute a material inducement to Existing Operator to enter into this Agreement and

2.5    Accounts Receivable.



                                                 8

        (a)     New Operator shall assume responsibility for the billing for and collection of

2.6    Payment of Operating Costs, Prorations and Deposits.

         (a)     Except as otherwise expressly provided herein, Existing Operator shall be
responsible for, and shall pay on a timely basis, claims or charges which are owed to third parties
arising from Existing Operator’s use, operation or control of the Facility, including payroll,
taxes, insurance premiums, utilities, including water, fuel, gas, oil, heat, electricity and other
utilities, operating charges, prepaid service contracts, amounts due under executory obligations,
amounts due to any third party vendors, including amounts due under any Operating
Agreements, and similar obligations for all periods prior to the Closing Date. In addition, with
respect to all agreements of Existing Operator that do not constitute Assumed Facility
Agreements, Existing Operator shall be responsible for, and shall pay on a timely basis, claims or
charges which are owed to third parties arising thereunder, for all periods prior to, on or after the
Closing Date.

        (b)     New Operator, to the extent it utilizes the services provided by third parties, shall
be responsible for, and shall pay on a timely basis, any claims or charges which are due to such
third parties arising from the use, operation or control of the Facility from and after the Closing
Date.

        (c)     Revenues and expenses pertaining to utility charges for the billing period in which
the Closing takes place, prepaid expenses and like items of revenue or expense attributable to the
Facility shall be prorated between Existing Operator and New Operator as of the Closing Date.
All such prorations shall be made on the basis of actual days elapsed in the relevant accounting
or revenue period and shall be based on the most recent information available to Existing


                                                 10

===== PAGE 140 =====
Operator. In general, such prorations shall be made so as to reimburse Existing Operator for
actual prepaid expense items, and to charge Existing Operator for prepaid revenue items, to the
extent that the same are attributable to periods after the Closing Date.

       (d)     To the extent any third party utility provider delivers final readings as of the
Closing Date, the Existing Operator shall be responsible for paying such final invoice amount,
which shall be reflected in the OTA Closing Statement as a debit to Existing Operator. Utility
charges that are not metered and read on the Closing Date shall be estimated based on prior
charges, and shall be re-prorated upon receipt of statements therefor.

        (e)    On the Closing Date, Existing Operator shall remove from the Facility any petty
cash and any other funds maintained at or for the Facility immediately prior to the Closing Date,
other than Resident Trust Funds, which shall be handled in the manner set forth in Section 2.3.

        (f)     If at any time on or after the Effective Date, Existing Operator pursues any real
estate or personal property tax appeals and such appeals result in a reduction or increase in real
estate and/or personal property taxes with respect to the Facility for such period, such reduction
or increase shall be prorated between Existing Operator and New Operator as of the Closing
Date, subject to adjustment following the Closing Date in accordance with this Section 2.6(f) and
Section 2.7 hereof. Furthermore, in the event that Existing Operator owes any amounts to third
parties in connection with any such appeal that results in a reduction or increase in real estate
and/or personal property taxes with respect to the Facility for the period in which the Closing
takes place, such costs shall be prorated between Existing Operator and New Operator in
proportion to the benefit of the applicable tax reduction or detriment of the applicable tax
increase that is realized as a result of such appeal by Existing Operator and New Operator,
respectively. If at any time on or after the Closing Date, and not subject to the three (3) month
limitation set forth in Section 2.7, there is any reduction or increase in real estate and/or personal
property taxes with respect to the Facility for the tax year in which the Closing occurs, as a result
of the transactions contemplated herein or otherwise, such reduction or increase shall be prorated
between Existing Operator and New Operator as of the Closing Date.

2.7     Future Settlement. All amounts owing from one party hereto to the other party hereto,
excluding amounts in respect of Section 2.3 hereof, that require adjustment after the Closing

Operator under Section 2.4 hereof and prorations or re-prorations of any claims or charges
according to Section 2.6 hereof regardless of whether such claims or charges are included in the

thereafter, a party hereto determines that any further adjustment is to be made, such party shall
submit a statement to the owing party setting forth any and all such items and the calculation of
the amounts due hereunder. Such statement shall be submitted with appropriate backup
materials. If amounts are owing from New Operator to Existing Operator, New Operator shall
have thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of such statement to tender payment to Existing
Operator or to question or dispute in writing any item thereon. If amounts are determined to be
owing from Existing Operator to New Operator, Existing Operator shall have thirty (30) days
from the date of receipt of such statement to tender payment to New Operator or to question or
dispute in writing any item thereon.

obligations or debts of Existing Operator, including, without limitation: (1) malpractice or other
tort claims, employment liability claims, or breach of contract claims, to the extent based on acts
or omissions of Existing Operator occurring prior to the Closing Date; (2) amounts due or that
may become due to Medicare, Medicaid, any fiscal intermediary, or any federal or state
Governmental Entity or any private third party payors on account of cost report adjustments or
other payment adjustments to the extent attributable prior to the Closing Date, or any other form
of reimbursement recoupment, recapture, adjustment, or overpayment attributable prior to the
Closing Date; (3) any accounts payable, taxes, or other obligation or liability of Existing
Operator to pay money incurred by the Existing Operator prior to the Closing Date; (4) liabilities
or obligations of the Existing Operator to its creditors, shareholders, members or owners; (5)
liabilities or obligations of the Existing Operator with respect to any Facility Agreements or
other agreements, acts, events or transactions occurring with respect to the Facility prior to the
Closing Date (other than obligations and liabilities under Assumed Facility Agreements, as
defined herein, that accrue or arise on or after the Effective Date); (6) any employee benefit

   “Facility Records” shall mean all of the books, records (including all current resident and

results, I-9s or other employee records that are produced and maintained by third party vendors.
   “Governmental Entity” shall mean any (a) federal, state, county or municipal government, or
city, town, borough, village, district or other jurisdiction; (b) governmental or quasi-
governmental entity of any nature (including any agency, branch, department, board,
commission, court, tribunal or other entity exercising governmental or quasi-governmental
powers); and (c) any body exercising, or entitled or purporting to exercise, any administrative,
executive, judicial, legislative, police, regulatory or taxing authority or power.
  “Health Care Requirements” shall mean, with respect to the Facility, all federal, state, county,
municipal and other governmental statutes, laws, rules, orders, regulations, ordinances,
judgments, decrees and injunctions or agreements, in each case, pertaining to or concerned with
the establishment, construction, ownership, operation, use or occupancy of the Facility or any
part thereof as a nursing facility and all regulations relating thereto, including all material rules,
orders, regulations and decrees of and agreements with Health Care Authorities as pertaining to
the Facility and the payment and/or reimbursement for services rendered or goods or materials
supplied at the Facility.
  “Legal Requirement” shall mean any federal, state, local municipal or other order, constitution,
law, ordinance, principle of comment law, code, regulation, or statute.
  “Material Adverse Effect” means, (a) following the Effective Date, the loss of any licensure,
certification or other material permit necessary to operate the Facility as a skilled nursing
facility, including the Facility having its Health Care License revoked, suspended, placed on
probation, or otherwise disciplined or limited, whether permanently or temporarily; (b) following
the Effective Date, the designation of a Facility as a SFF; (c) following the Effective Date, the
decertification or other action of Existing Operator or the Facility from or with respect to
participation under Medicare, Medicaid or any other governmental health care program,
including being suspended or limited from, or otherwise deemed ineligible for, or having any
denial of payment or admissions or other limitation imposed with respect to, whether
permanently or temporarily, participation in the Medicare and/or Medicaid reimbursement
program; (d) the issuance of a level “I” or higher survey deficiency that is not deemed to be
cured and in compliance by the Closing Date; and (e) the identification of any deficiencies as a
result of a survey that takes place not less than thirty (30) days prior to the Closing that have not
been cured and deemed to be in compliance by the applicable Health Care Authority, which

substantially the same terms set forth in Purchaser’s term sheet or negotiated loan documents with such

lender, provided that New Operator has used its commercially reasonable efforts to cause its
lender to close over any such survey deficiency that does not otherwise constitute a Material
Adverse Effect under subparts (a) – (d) of this definition. For clarity, a survey few than 30 days
prior to the Closing Date will not be deemed to trigger a Material Adverse Effect as defined in
the preceding subpart (e).
  “Minimum Data Set” shall mean a federal assessment system which contains a standardized
set of essential clinical and functional status measures.
  “Resident Census Report” shall mean a true, correct and complete schedule (provided in
accordance with all applicable Health Care Requirements related to privacy) which accurately
and completely sets forth the occupancy status of the Facility, the average daily rate and other
charges payable with respect thereto, the class of payment or reimbursement (i.e., private, third-
party payor, Medicare, and Veterans Administration), the average monthly census of the Facility
and its occupancy rate.
  “Resident Trust Funds” shall mean the funds held in trust by Existing Operator for residents at
the Facility.

CHARITY CARE POLICY & PROCEDURE

South County Nursing & Rehabilitation Center

Purpose:

It shall be the policy of South County Nursing & Rehabilitation Center (“SCNRC”) to provide
free care to Residents on a case-by-case basis, based on facility financial ability.

Qualifying Residents:

SCRNC will provide free care to those Residents who have a medical need for SCRNC’s
services and who meet the charity care guidelines as outlined herein (“Qualifying Residents”).
Accordingly, Qualifying Residents will be those uninsured or underinsured Residents with
incomes up to 125% of the Federal Poverty Limits and who are without readily available funds
that could be used to pay for their care. (Qualifying Residents must have applied for any
governmental assistance programs for which they qualify. If a Qualifying Resident is not
eligible for governmental assistance or is denied governmental assistance, such Resident may
apply for charity care).

Charity Care Policy:

SCRNC agrees it will neither bill Qualifying Residents for services directly supplied by SCRNC
nor collect any fees for provision of such services. Services that are provided under contract
with an outside provider shall not be eligible for charity care and will be billed in the customary
manner, unless otherwise explicitly agreed in writing by the outside provider.

Monitoring:

A summary of charity care provided will be drafted and provided to management on an annual
basis.

OPS103 Center Quality Assurance Performance Improvement
(QAPI) Process
    MANUAL TITLE:           Center Operations Policies and Procedures
    POLICY TITLE:           OPS103 Center Quality Assurance Performance Improvement (QAPI)
                            Process
    APPLICATION:            Genesis HealthCare Centers
    EFFECTIVE DATE:         01/30/17
    REVIEW DATE:            01/30/17
    REVISION DATE:          02/13/17

POLICY
The Center is committed to incorporating the principles of Quality Assurance and Performance
Improvement (QAPI) into all aspects of the Center work processes, service lines, and
departments. All staff and stakeholders are involved in QAPI to improve the quality of life and quality
of care that our patients experience.
PURPOSE
To standardize the Center’s approach to QAPI culture and processes by implementing the following
key elements.
     The QAPI program is ongoing, integrated, data driven, and comprehensive, addressing all aspects
      of care, quality of life, and patient centered rights and choice.
     The Center Executive Director (CED) leads the Center’s QAPI processes and involves all
      departments, staff, and stakeholders— balancing a culture of safety, quality, and patient
      centeredness.
     The QAPI processes and improvements are based on evidence, drawing data from multiple
      sources, prioritizing improvement opportunities, and benchmarking results against developed
      targets.
     Improvement Activities (IAs) and Performance Improvement Projects (PIPs) are the structure and
      means through which identified problem areas are addressed with data analysis, process
      improvements, and ongoing monitoring whenever necessary using an interdisciplinary team.
     The learning through applied QAPI is continuous, systematic, and organized.
PROCESS
1. The CED directs the development and documentation of the Center QAPI Plan, including an
   Annual QAPI Calendar, and is responsible for development, maintenance, and ongoing evaluation
   of an active and effective QAPI Committee (QAPIC).
2. The QAPIC:
        2.1 Functions under the authority of the CED and the Governing Body;
        2.2 Is composed of the following individuals:
              2.2.1 CED,
              2.2.2 Center Nurse Executive,
              2.2.3 Medical Director,
              2.2.4 The Infection Preventionist, or designee,
              2.2.5 A representative from each department, including at least one CNA, and
              2.2.6 Where Excellence Teams (standing subcommittees that support Excellence Pillars)
                    are in place, the Leader (co-leaders) from each Team,

===== PAGE 206 =====
            2.2.7 Other representatives such as partner providers (Genesis Rehab Services, hospice,
                  home health, Genesis Physician Services, HCS), patients and/or family members,
                  physicians, divisional support leaders as appropriate (or defined by state
                  regulations) to provide further insight and resource management;
     2.3 Meets at least 10 times annually, preferably monthly, to monitor quality within the Center,
         identify issues, and develop and implement appropriate plans of action to correct identified
         quality issues; and
     2.4 Has a recording secretary designated by the CED.
3. The responsibilities of the QAPIC are to:
     3.1 Develop/implement an effective QAPI program.
     3.2 Follow a structured agenda to conduct monthly meetings.
            3.2.1 All members must sign the QAPIC Sign-in Sheet.
     3.3 Assess, evaluate, and identify potential improvement opportunities based on:
            3.3.1 Current reviews of core systems (identified on the Annual QAPI Calendar) for the
                  month;
            3.3.2 All current regulatory on-site assessments, including plans of correction, both
                  state/federal surveys and peer review surveys including a review of the plan of
                  correction;
            3.3.3 Adverse events since the past meeting including prevention opportunities,
                  investigation, and corrective actions;
            3.3.4 Results and activities of the Infection Prevention and Control Program;
            3.3.5 Potential issues identified through Routine QAPI activities such as, but not limited
                  to, family comments, patient requests, staff suggestions, grievances.
     3.4 Review, analyze trends, and identify potential improvement opportunities for the following,
         based on the Analysis and Action Plan process completed prior to the QAPIC.
            3.4.1 Center Strategic Performance Plan by reviewing trends against annual goals
                  and company comparisons. Elements of the Strategic Performance Plan reviews
                  are scheduled on the Annual QAPI Calendar.
            3.4.2 Publically-Reported Measures where trends are worsening or levels have
                  exceeded targets. Elements of the publicly reported measure reviews are
                  scheduled on the Annual QAPI Calendar.
            3.4.3 Other Performance Data where trends are worsening or levels have exceeded
                  targets. Elements of the performance data reviews are scheduled on the Annual
                  QAPI Calendar.
            3.4.4 Lab/Pharmacy/Medical Director Performance data (quarterly).
            3.4.5 Systems/Reports for contracted services at a minimum of, but not limited to,
                  quarterly.
     3.5 Identify and prioritize areas of improvement, assign improvement activities and PIPs (PI
          Teams) where needed, and track progress.
            3.5.1 QAPIC prioritizes all issues recommended for improvement based on impact to
                  quality of care and quality of life including high risk, high volume, or problem
                  prone areas from #3.2 and #3.3 above. Issues may be recommended for an
                  improvement activity (requires limited time and staff involvement) or an
                  interdisciplinary, Center-wide PI Team that will develop a charter and use
                  systematic methodology to identify, test, and sustain the improvement.

===== PAGE 207 =====
            3.5.2 All PI Teams use a systematic approach for problem analysis, cause identification,
                  solution brainstorming, process change action trials, outcome measurement,
                  improvement spread, and process monitoring.
            3.5.3 The QAPIC tracks progress and discusses success/barriers for all Improvement
                  Activities and PIPs to ascertain support, resources, and breakthrough ideas.
     3.6 Record minutes of all meetings.
            3.6.1 All minutes must include the following for each topic discussed:
                   3.6.1.1 Discussion,
                   3.6.1.2 Recommendations/actions,
                   3.6.1.3 Persons responsible/date due.
            3.6.2 All materials circulated prior to and discussed at the meeting are referred to in the
                  minutes and filed separately (refer to #4.1.4).
            3.6.3 Distribute meeting minutes to meeting participants for review and approval at the
                  next meeting.
            3.6.4 Post meeting minutes in the designated location within the Centers and make
                  available for review by the Regional Vice President and Clinical Quality Specialist.
     3.7 Promote full employee participation in identifying and improving key processes.
            3.7.1 QAPIC ensures education for all staff to facilitate understanding of QAPI program
                  and processes, and systems to engage staff in participation in identifying
                  improvement opportunities and participating in PI teams.
            3.7.2 Assures QAPI program and processes are presented at staff orientation and at
                  annual mandatory in-service programs.
            3.7.3 Ensures staff are invited, encouraged, and welcomed to participate in PI Teams
                  and improvement activities during their work schedules.
            3.7.4 Communicate progress and results of improvement projects to entire staff.
4. Documentation of QAPI activities is filed by month for a period of one year in the QAPI Binder.
     4.1 Documentation for each meeting must include:
            4.1.1 Agenda
            4.1.2 Sign-in sheet
            4.1.3 Minutes
            4.1.4 Updated Improvement Log
                   4.1.4.1 Attachments such as completed QAPI Improvement Tools, handouts
                           distributed at the meeting, and all other reports or tools used for Quality
                           Improvement activities are filed in a separate binder.
     4.2 All QAPI tools, reports, findings, plans of action, etc. are confidential quality assurance
         information and are filed separately from other committee documentation in a secured file
         or area. Surveyors and other regulatory agencies may have access to QAPI improvement
         documentation as stipulated by regulation.
     4.3 At the end of each calendar year, the manual is emptied, its contents archived, and a new
         year of documentation is started.
     4.4 The QAPI program is evaluated annually to determine its effectiveness in improving quality
         of care and quality of life, operational sustainability, employee and customer satisfaction.
         The annual evaluation is reviewed by the Governing Body.

      Central Quality Assurance Performance Improvement (QAPI) Sharepoint
